reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its norm and Borel measurable structure, and let V:E→ℝ, α,β∈[0,∞), and η∈ℝ. Assume α>0, η>0, V is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable, and for every x,v∈E, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖². Define μ to be normalized exponential weighting of Lebesgue measure by −V. Let J be the pushforward of μ⊗γ under (x,g)↦(x,x+√η g), where γ is the standard centered Gaussian on E. Define the continuous-linear-functional-valued function s by s(y,u)=−(1/2)DV((y+u)/2)−(1/(4η))⟨y−u,·⟩. There exist Markov kernels R and S from E to E with the following simultaneous properties. First, R disintegrates the swapped joint measure swap₍*₎J conditional on its first coordinate; thus, in the joint-coordinate notation (X,Y) for J, R is a conditional distribution of X given Y. Second, for every y∈E, S(y) is the pushforward of R(y) under x↦2x−y. Third, for every y∈E, S(y) is normalized exponential weighting of Lebesgue measure in u by −V((y+u)/2)−‖y−u‖²/(8η). Finally, for every smooth compactly supported real-valued function f on E and every y∈E, both u↦s(y,u) and u↦f(u)s(y,u) are Bochner integrable under S(y), and F(z)=∫f(u)S(z)(du) has a Fréchet derivative at y equal to ∫f(u)s(y,u)S(y)(du)−(∫f(u)S(y)(du))(∫s(y,u)S(y)(du)). Equivalently, its derivative applied to h∈E is ∫f(u)s(y,u)[h]S(y)(du)−(∫f(u)S(y)(du))(∫s(y,u)[h]S(y)(du)).
The same R,S work for every f,y. The explicit fiber identities hold everywhere, although disintegration itself identifies a conditional version relative to the marginal. This is existence of a suitable version, not a statement about every conditional version. Local μ,J,s are definitions rather than hypotheses. No positive-dimension or separate α≤β premise occurs. There is no asserted uniqueness, measure-valued or operator-norm differentiability, continuous derivative, higher derivative, arbitrary measurable test extension or quantitative derivative bound. The unnormalized score need not have zero mean; the formula centers it. The exact coefficients are √η, 2, 1/2, 1/(8η) and 1/(4η), with kernels selected before the tests.
